description: The acceptance names test-accepting-authority but is signed with — and carries — a substituted key. The signature is internally consistent, so key binding passes; role verification against the caller's authorityTrustList (the genuine authority key) fails. Key binding and role are reported separately, and only key binding gates: role is undecidable from the package alone — without a caller-supplied trust list there is nothing to decide membership against — so a substituted key is reported and the package stays accepted. This is what the self-attestation trust model costs on the acceptance side, exactly as boundary/reauthored-package-issuer-substitution is what it costs on the issuer side.
